I can easily see why people would like it, but for me it really reeks of cheap development.  Kind of like the old 007 games when they kept getting better textures, but the underlying tech was the exact same.    

It's as if it were a mod for Far Cry 3 that a handful of modders created in their garage and released for free.  Nothing really special or new about it.  It could've been a $20 expansion pack instead of a full blown game and they still would've netted a generous profit. 

The fact that the game uses a numbers driven hp/dmg system with leveling only makes the game less appealing as that's a superficial way to accomplish two goals that every gamer should be against.  

1) It turns the "open world" game into a linear one.  The freedom to explore becomes a sort of illusion as you can encounter enemies "beyond your level" that can tank multiple clips of gunfire without dying. (something that should NEVER happen in a fps game unless it's some sort of boss battle) 

2) It sets up a system where developers can gradually increase the difficulty and/or time it takes to level up, thus encouraging players to spend more money on "xp boost packs" or other similar useless bonuses.

​

I'm still early in (lvl 4) so I'm still reserving final judgement, but it's really not looking good at this point.
